chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Sama'a ibn Mihran who said:

I asked him about the virgin girl menstruating for the first time, when she sits (menstruating) during one month for two days, and during another month for three days, and it varies for her — her menstruation not occurring during the month with the same number of days.

He said: For her is that she sits (in menstruation) and leaves the salat as long as she continues to see the blood, as long as she does not exceed ten (days). So when two months coincide with the same number of days, then those are her (regular) days.

key_terms.أَيَّامُهَا: Her days — referring to the established regular days of the menstrual cycle once it has stabilized
key_terms.الْجَارِيَةُ الْبِكْرُ: The virgin girl — a young woman who has not yet had sexual intercourse; in the jurisprudential context, a girl experiencing her first menstruation
key_terms.طَمْث: Menstrual blood (haydh); the classical Arabic term used in fiqh texts for menstruation, distinct from istihadha (irregular bleeding)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling for a virgin girl whose first menstruation is irregular in duration?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through Sama'a ibn Mihran from the Imam, addresses the Islamic legal ruling for a young virgin girl experiencing her first menstrual cycles when the duration is irregular. The Imam rules that she should abstain from prayer (salat) throughout any bleeding period, provided it does not exceed ten days — the maximum for haydh. The regular cycle is established once two consecutive months show the same number of bleeding days. This is a foundational ruling in Shia fiqh for determining a woman's menstrual cycle (haydh) when it is initially irregular, responding to the practical concern that newly menstruating girls often experience variable cycles before they stabilize.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Usman Bin Isa, from Sama’at Bin Mihran who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the virgin girl menstruating the first time, so she sits (menstruating) during the month for two days, and during (another) month, for three days, and it is different upon her, her menstruating not occurring upon her during the month with the same number of days.

Heasws said: ‘For her is that she sits (awaiting) and leaves the Salaat for as long as she sees the blood, as long as she does not exceed the ten (days). So when the two months coincide with the number of days as being the same, so those are her (regular) days’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ‘Uthman ibn ’Isa from Sama‘ah ibn Mehran who has said the following:

“I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a young girl who experiences Hayd (menses) for the first time. In one month she experiences for two days and in the second month for three days and so they are not certain days of known duration every month.

He (the Imam) said, ‘ She must deal with it like Hayd (menses) and stop performing Salah (prayer) as long as there is discharge which is not more than ten days. If the duration of her Hayd (menses) in two months remains the same, this establishes a pattern for her Hayd (menses).”’
